result_text:
I found 4 issues in `96305ff..2be1432`. Three are bugs that should be fixed before merging and one is minor. No CLAUDE.md rule is broken by the diff. I traced the logic by reading the code; I did not run the tests.

```json
[
  {
    "file": "src/domain/day-timeline.ts",
    "line": 505,
    "summary": "The schedule can list a stop with no selected place after a drive that starts before it, so `scheduleOf()` is not in time order as the design promises. In `#addSelected`, waiting stops are always added after the drive. This goes wrong whenever the waiting stop's time is earlier than the drive's end, which happens when its set time comes before the next selected stop's earliest arrival. Fix: add waiting stops whose time is before the drive's start ahead of the free time and drive, or limit the 'after the drive' rule to stops whose time is at or after the drive's end.",
    "failure_scenario": "A selected stop ends at 2:00. Next is an unselected stop set for 2:30, then a selected stop with a 60-minute drive. The output is drive 2:00–3:00, then the unselected stop at 2:30, then the stop at 3:00. The 2:30 entry comes after an entry that ends at 3:00, so the schedule is out of time order.",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "src/domain/weather-out-of-date.ts",
    "line": 729,
    "summary": "Seasonal weather text is never marked out of date once the trip has no dates. `datesStillFit` calls `dates.every(...)`, which returns true for an empty list. `datesOf()` returns [] when the start date is cleared, so the old text still counts as current. A forecast in the same case is flagged, because its length check fails. Fix: when `dates` is empty but `written` isn't, return false.",
    "failure_scenario": "Weather is written as seasonal averages for 2027-05-13..16, then the user clears the start date. `isWeatherOutOfDate` returns false, so the UI shows the old text as current and the `weatherOutOfDate` note is never given.",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "src/domain/calendar.ts",
    "line": 316,
    "summary": "Stale drive times can be used when a day's start or end place has changed. `#driveMinutesOf` only checks that the leg was routed through the day's current selected stops. It never compares `leg.routedFromPlace` and `leg.routedToPlace` with `fromPlaceOf()` and `toPlaceOf()`. If lodging or the start or end place changes partway through a write, the old segment times are used as if they were current. Fix: also require both ends to match by ID before trusting the times.",
    "failure_scenario": "Partway through a write, a stay's lodging changes before the leg is re-routed. `StopsService.approveOpeningHours()` calls `openTimeInMinutesOf`, which uses the old leg's segment times. The stop's arrival is wrong, so the recorded open minutes are wrong.",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "src/domain/day-timeline.ts",
    "line": 436,
    "summary": "An entry that crosses the second midnight shows a start time but no end time. `toScheduleEntry` converts each end on its own, and `scheduleTimeAt` returns null at 2880 minutes or more. `#push` blanks both times when either is unknown, but this path doesn't, and stop entries never go through `#push`. Fix: in `toScheduleEntry`, set both times to null when either one is null, matching `#push`.",
    "failure_scenario": "A stop starts at 11:30 p.m. the next day (minute 2850) with a 60-minute visit, so it ends at minute 2910. Its `ScheduleEntry` has a `startTime` of 11:30 p.m. and an `endTime` of null. The UI then shows a known start with 'time set once a place is picked', even though the place is selected.",
    "severity": "nit"
  }
]
```

findings.summary: The schedule can list a stop with no selected place after a drive that starts before it, so `scheduleOf()` is not in time order as the design promises. In `#addSelected`, waiting stops are always added after the drive. This goes wrong whenever the waiting stop's time is earlier than the drive's end, which happens when its set time comes before the next selected stop's earliest arrival. Fix: add waiting stops whose time is before the drive's start ahead of the free time and drive, or limit the 'after the drive' rule to stops whose time is at or after the drive's end.
findings.failure_scenario: A selected stop ends at 2:00. Next is an unselected stop set for 2:30, then a selected stop with a 60-minute drive. The output is drive 2:00–3:00, then the unselected stop at 2:30, then the stop at 3:00. The 2:30 entry comes after an entry that ends at 3:00, so the schedule is out of time order.

findings.summary: Seasonal weather text is never marked out of date once the trip has no dates. `datesStillFit` calls `dates.every(...)`, which returns true for an empty list. `datesOf()` returns [] when the start date is cleared, so the old text still counts as current. A forecast in the same case is flagged, because its length check fails. Fix: when `dates` is empty but `written` isn't, return false.
findings.failure_scenario: Weather is written as seasonal averages for 2027-05-13..16, then the user clears the start date. `isWeatherOutOfDate` returns false, so the UI shows the old text as current and the `weatherOutOfDate` note is never given.

findings.summary: Stale drive times can be used when a day's start or end place has changed. `#driveMinutesOf` only checks that the leg was routed through the day's current selected stops. It never compares `leg.routedFromPlace` and `leg.routedToPlace` with `fromPlaceOf()` and `toPlaceOf()`. If lodging or the start or end place changes partway through a write, the old segment times are used as if they were current. Fix: also require both ends to match by ID before trusting the times.
findings.failure_scenario: Partway through a write, a stay's lodging changes before the leg is re-routed. `StopsService.approveOpeningHours()` calls `openTimeInMinutesOf`, which uses the old leg's segment times. The stop's arrival is wrong, so the recorded open minutes are wrong.

findings.summary: An entry that crosses the second midnight shows a start time but no end time. `toScheduleEntry` converts each end on its own, and `scheduleTimeAt` returns null at 2880 minutes or more. `#push` blanks both times when either is unknown, but this path doesn't, and stop entries never go through `#push`. Fix: in `toScheduleEntry`, set both times to null when either one is null, matching `#push`.
findings.failure_scenario: A stop starts at 11:30 p.m. the next day (minute 2850) with a 60-minute visit, so it ends at minute 2910. Its `ScheduleEntry` has a `startTime` of 11:30 p.m. and an `endTime` of null. The UI then shows a known start with 'time set once a place is picked', even though the place is selected.
